cur-fossil-olduvai.dateNote: On 17 July 1959 Mary Leakey found the skull of "Nutcracker Man" (Paranthropus boisei) in this Tanzanian gorge. Its layers hold about 2 million years of stone tools and bones; the skull is about 1.8 million years old.

cur-find-olorgesailie.dateNote: Tools about 320,000 years old from this Kenyan basin, made of obsidian carried from far away, with lumps of colouring pigment: some of the earliest signs of trade and colour use (Brooks et al. and Potts et al., Science, 2018).

cur-find-panga-ya-saidi.dateNote: A cave in coastal Kenya where a child of about three, now called Mtoto, was laid in a grave about 78,000 years ago: Africa's oldest known human burial (Martinón-Torres et al., Nature, 2021).

cur-find-kalambo.dateNote: Waterlogged wood by the falls in Zambia includes two logs joined by a cut notch, about 476,000 years old: the oldest known wooden structure, older than our own species (Barham et al., Nature, 2023).

cur-find-nyayanga.dateNote: On the shore of Lake Victoria, Kenya, Oldowan stone tools about 2.6-3.0 million years old lie with butchered hippo bones and teeth of Paranthropus, a cousin of our ancestors (Plummer et al., Science, 2023).
